content:
alex: Heads-up — I'm going to merge the notify-backpressure debounce change into the console UI branch today. need quick input on API shape + UX for per-tenant backoff.

sam: Are we making debounce a per-route override or only per-tenant?

maria: My vote is per-tenant with per-route override opt-in. telemetry needs to emit enough fields to detect missed signals.

jon: API sketch: `POST /v2/notify/policies` body -> `{ tenant_id, debounce_ms?, mode: "immediate|soft|hard", thresholds: [...] }`  (soft = sampled notifications, hard = suppression)

alex: main concern: raising debounce hides spikes. we should surface synthetic metrics so operators can detect when alerts drop to 0.

sam: Proposal: 3-tier model like jon said. UI exposes toggle + short explainer. default for most tenants = soft.

maria: Telemetry fields I'd like: `event=notify_attempt`, attrs `{ tenant_id, route, sample_rate, debounce_ms, suppressed_count }`. also `last_suppressed_at` timestamp.

jon: impl note: runtime currently has token-bucket per-tenant; per-route buckets are doable but memory-heavy. we can start per-tenant + route heuristics (hashing) then opt-in per-route later.

alex: agree on incremental path. start per-tenant rollout so we can measure suppressed_count globally, then flip per-route when we see memory/benefit tradeoff.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated for `notify-backpressure:v2` -> 5% tenant traffic, started by @alex

sam: :thumbsup: migration question — existing SLO rules store thresholds as floats. new API adds `debounce_ms` optional. plan to backfill `0` for old tenants?

maria: yes backfill 0. UX idea: show a `quieting` badge on SLO cards when suppression is active; clicking opens modal with history (suppressed_count timeline + last_suppressed_at).

jon: API versioning thought: v1->v2 additive is fine but let's include `compat_mode` boolean default false — safety toggle to preserve current behavior for customers who want no suppression.

alex: checklist before merge: 1) telemetry spec (fields + sample rates) 2) API spec + examples 3) UX mock for badge/modal 4) canary config 5) runbook update for ops 6) a small eval to ensure no SLOs silently degrade

sam: I'll draft a 1-pager RFC + attach mock. will call out memory impact for per-route.

alex: thanks — leaning incremental: per-tenant rollout + rich telemetry to detect signal loss. i'll update the PR and ping infra for resource estimate.

maria: ping me for the telemetry schema and a quick mock review.

jon: adding a test hook: emit `suppressed_count` as a gauge so alerting rules can target suppression regressions.

alex: perfect. merging after RFC + telemetry spec.

sam: ack, thanks everyone.
